Conservation Planner/GIS Specialist

Location:
Western or Central New York (Hybrid)* 
Employment Type:
Full-time (Part-time considered)
Compensation:
$65,000-$75,000 based on experience, plus benefits
Preferred Start Date:
October 5, 2026 

*
Candidates located within reasonable driving distance of Batavia, New York are encouraged to apply. Regular virtual collaboration is expected, along with periodic in-person meetings, project site visits, community meetings, and team events.

Applications will be reviewed as they are received. Priority will be given to applications received by September 18th. See below for how to apply.

About the Role

CC Environment & Planning is seeking a Conservation Planner to support our growing portfolio of conservation, environmental, and community planning projects across New York State. The Conservation Planner will work at the intersection of ecology, land-use planning, and Geographic Information Systems (GIS), helping communities and project partners understand natural resources, identify conservation priorities, and develop practical strategies that balance environmental protection with land-use and community needs. This role is ideal for someone with a strong background in ecology and natural resource management who enjoys applying science and spatial analysis to real-world planning decisions. The position will include GIS analysis and spatial modeling, interactive and web-based mapping, research, technical writing, conservation planning, and collaboration with municipalities, agencies, conservation organizations, and other project partners. 

Key Responsibilities

Conservation & Environmental Planning

Support the preparation of Natural Resource Inventories, Open Space Plans, Comprehensive Plans, conservation plans, climate resilience plans, and related planning documents
Assist in identifying conservation priorities, important natural areas, ecological corridors, and opportunities for resource protection
Help translate ecological and natural resource information into practical planning recommendations and implementation strategies
Support development of conservation goals, policies, priority actions, and planning recommendations

GIS & Spatial Analysis

Conduct GIS-based natural resource, conservation, and land-use analyses using ArcGIS Pro and related tools
Compile, organize, evaluate, and maintain spatial datasets from federal, state, regional, and local sources
Prepare clear and accurate GIS maps, figures, and other visual materials for technical reports and public presentations
Assist with management and quality control of project GIS databases
Develop interactive web maps, ArcGIS StoryMaps, and other web-based GIS products to communicate natural resource, conservation, and planning information to clients, stakeholders, and the public.

Conduct GIS-based suitability, prioritization, and weighted-overlay analyses to support conservation planning, including development of Open Space Indices, conservation priority areas, and recommended conservation actions.

Translate multiple ecological, land-use, and community datasets into clear spatial models and decision-support tools.

Ecological & Natural Resource Analysis

Evaluate resources including wetlands, streams, riparian corridors, forests, wildlife habitat, soils, floodplains, water resources, and other ecological features
Review available environmental studies, natural resource datasets, and technical information
Assist with integrating field observations and ecological data into GIS analyses and planning recommendations

Research, Writing, and Community Engagement 

Prepare technical summaries, planning documents, reports, tables, figures, and public-facing materials
Support community workshops, stakeholder meetings, advisory committees, and public presentations
Coordinate with municipal officials, planning boards, conservation advisory councils, agencies, nonprofit organizations, consultants, and other project partners
Assist project managers with research, project coordination, meeting preparation, and deliverable development

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor’s degree in ecology, environmental science, natural resources, or related field 
Proficiency with ArcGIS Pro and Microsoft 365 
Experience using GIS for spatial analysis beyond basic map production, including suitability, prioritization, weighted-overlay, or other multi-criteria analyses
Experience communicating directly with clients, partners, and agencies 
Ability to locate, evaluate, manage, and interpret environmental and land-use datasets
Ability to manage multiple assignments and work collaboratively as part of a multidisciplinary project team
Strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills 
Understanding of land-use practices and the relationship between development, conservation, and natural resource protection
Strong technical writing, research, and communication skills
Ability to interpret scientific and technical information and communicate it clearly to non-technical audiences

Preferred

Strong working knowledge of: 

Aquatic resource delineation and permitting
Ecological surveys and habitat assessment 
Restoration and natural resource management 

Experience preparing Natural Resource Inventories, Open Space Plans, Comprehensive Plans, watershed plans, climate resilience plans, or similar planning documents
Experience with public outreach, stakeholder engagement, or municipal committee meetings 
Familiarity with New York State GIS and environmental datasets, including information available from NYSDEC, NYS GIS Clearinghouse, NY Natural Heritage Program, FEMA, USGS, USDA NRCS, and other agencies
Experience with ArcGIS Online, ArcGIS StoryMaps, web maps, dashboards, or similar interactive GIS communication tools
Experience developing conservation prioritization models, Open Space Indices, suitability analyses, or other GIS-based decision-support tools

What We’re Looking For

This role is best suited for someone who is curious, analytical, organized, and interested in how ecological science can inform better land-use and conservation decisions. You are comfortable moving between GIS analysis, ecological research, technical writing, and community planning. You enjoy working with maps and data but can also step back and understand the larger landscape and planning context. The successful candidate will be able to recognize important ecological relationships, organize complex information, communicate technical concepts clearly, and help turn natural resource information into realistic recommendations that communities and decision-makers can use.

What It’s Like to Work at CC Environment & Planning

At CC Environment & Planning, we’re a small, mission-driven consulting firm doing big things. In partnership with North Country Ecological Services (NCES), we’ve expanded our ecological capacity to take on a growing portfolio of restoration, permitting, and planning projects across New York State and beyond. Our team thrives on collaboration, curiosity, and action. We work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment where flexibility, resourcefulness, and a positive attitude go a long way. No two days are the same — and that’s exactly how we like it.

When you join us, you’ll be part of a nimble, supportive team that values diverse perspectives, trusts its people, and invests in their growth. We’re looking for team members who are not only technically strong, but also adaptable, proactive, and energized by meaningful work that makes a difference.

Flexible work schedules and a mix of remote, hybrid, and in-person collaboration
Full benefits package including health insurance, retirement, and generous PTO
Opportunities to cross-train and grow in new skills and leadership
A culture that supports autonomy, creativity, and professional development
Direct engagement with projects that restore landscapes, support communities, and shape a more resilient future

If you love rolling up your sleeves, solving real-world problems, and working with people who are passionate about the environment — you’ll fit right in.

How to Apply:

Send a cover letter, resume, and any relevant work samples to Angelina White, Senior Planner at awhite@ccenvironment.com. Applications reviewed on a rolling basis.

Work Sample ( Required ):
Please include a relevant work sample that demonstrates your GIS, conservation planning, ecological analysis, or technical communication skills. Examples appropriate for this role include:

A GIS map or spatial analysis you developed
A Natural Resource Inventory, Open Space Plan, conservation plan, or similar planning document you contributed to
A technical memorandum, report, or planning document you authored
A conservation prioritization, suitability, or land-use analysis
A research or academic project demonstrating applied ecology, conservation biology, or natural resource planning
An interactive web map, ArcGIS StoryMap, dashboard, or similar GIS-based public communication product
A conservation prioritization, suitability, weighted-overlay, Open Space Index, or other spatial decision-support analysis

Applicants may redact confidential or proprietary information from work samples.

Equal Opportunity Employer

CC Environment & Planning is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We encourage applicants of all backgrounds to apply.

Proficiency in statistical programming languages (e.g., R, SPSS, Stata, SAS), data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI), and database applications.
Demonstrated experience leading the preparation of research manuscripts and securing grant funding.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills with ability to effectively communicate with faculty and staff.
Detail oriented and ability to organize tasks and prioritize work with minimal supervision.
Ability to multi-task and work cooperatively with others.

Experience working with and accessing local, state and national data sets (e.g., Texas health data, NHANES, WHI, Framingham Heart Study, etc.).

Job Summary

The University of Michigan School of Social Work's Office of Field Education seeks a Field Placement and Program Coordinator to support student field placements, develop relationships with community-based agencies, and contribute to the effective administration of the Office of Field Education.

This position combines field-placement coordination (approximately 60%) with program and administrative support (approximately 40%). The successful candidate will bring a student-centered approach, sound professional judgment, strong organizational skills, and a commitment to social work education, community engagement, and social work values and ethics.

The coordinator will work collaboratively with students, field faculty, School of Social Work colleagues, and community partners. Responsibilities include identifying and engaging potential field sites, facilitating student placement processes, responding to student questions, coordinating office operations, and supporting projects and initiatives of the Office of Field Education. The relative distribution of responsibilities may fluctuate during peak placement and program periods.

Field Placement Coordination (60%)

Identify, recruit, and support prospective community-based field education sites.

Develop field-placement opportunities that align with student learning needs and Office of Field Education requirements.
Facilitate student placements with field agencies using established matching processes and protocols.

Collaborate with the Director and Assistant Director of Field Education on projects involving:
agency recruitment and development
agency review and vetting
student support services
placement-process software and system enhancements
curricular or program innovations

Track project activities, timelines, and deliverables.
Support other Office of Field Education initiatives and special projects as assigned.

Program and Administrative Support (40%)

Provide welcoming and professional front-office support to students, faculty, staff, community partners, and visitors.

Provide administrative and clerical support to the Director and Assistant Director of Field Education, field faculty, and other members of the office.
Prepare and distribute reports, agendas, correspondence, and other materials.
Record, edit, and distribute minutes for weekly team meetings and other meetings as assigned.
Draft, format, proofread, and manage written communications.
Create and maintain organized electronic and physical filing systems.
Coordinate room reservations and meeting logistics.
Order, maintain, and monitor office supplies and equipment.
Assist with purchasing, expense reconciliation, email communications, and other office processes as assigned.
Help maintain a welcoming, professional, accessible, and organized office environment.
Handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion.
Balance multiple priorities in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.
Perform other related duties and projects as assigned.

Excellent interpersonal, written and oral communication skills.
Demonstrated ability to provide responsive service to individuals from varied backgrounds and experiences.
Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to coordinate multiple responsibilities and deadlines.
Demonstrated ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, solve problems, and contribute effectively within a team.
Ability to understand, follow, and recommend improvements to complex administrative processes.
Demonstrated ability to build effective working relationships with all stakeholders.

Proficiency with Google Workspace applications, particularly Google Docs, Google Sheets, and Google Slides.

Experience in field education, student services, higher education, social work, human services, community engagement, or interagency collaboration.

new_jobs.title: Senior Program Coordinator, Medical Scientist Training Program
new_jobs.description:
WHY UT SOUTHWESTERN?

With over 75 years of excellence in Dallas-Fort Worth, Texas, UT Southwestern is committed to excellence, innovation, teamwork, and compassion. As a world-renowned medical and research center, we strive to provide the best possible care, resources, and benefits for our valued employees. Ranked as the number 1 hospital in Dallas-Fort Worth according to U.S. News & World Report, we invest in you with opportunities for career growth and development to align with your future goals. Our highly competitive benefits package offers healthcare, PTO and paid holidays, on-site childcare, wage, merit increases and so much more. We invite you to be a part of the UT Southwestern team where you'll discover a culture of teamwork, professionalism, and a rewarding career!

Job Summary

The UT Southwestern Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences is recruiting a full-time Senior Program Coordinator for the Perot Family Scholars Medical Scientist Training Program. The program’s mission is to train physician–scientists who lead innovative research programs, translate discovery to patient care, and shape the future of medicine through scientific leadership. Students in the program obtain dual M.D. and Ph.D. degrees. To support the continued growth of the program, we are recruiting a senior program coordinator to join the program leadership team, which consists of a faculty director, two co-directors, and multiple other supporting roles within the Graduate School.

The Senior Program Coordinator will be responsible for coordinating recruitment, admissions, and onboarding efforts for the program, in addition to generating data insights to guide program decision-making. This role will manage student progression through the dual-degree program, engage with leadership to implement new program initiatives, work collaboratively with other Graduate School staff to meet program objectives, and liaise with leaders and staff of other University departments. Specific day-to-day tasks include managing student enrollment, developing student outcomes tracking system, financial oversight of the program budget, management of NIH T32 award including drafting annual reports and renewal applications, coordinating/hosting program seminars and meetings, developing program recruitment materials, and engaging with prospective applicants.

Candidates with prior experience with MSTP, NIH T32 grants, and familiarity with both clinical and basic science research environments will be given strong consideration. A successful candidate will be a self-starter who can design and implement new program initiatives. They will be able to represent the program nationally at recruitment and networking events and institutionally to executive leadership. They will be strong team-players who can work collaboratively with staff, faculty, and students to achieve program goals. They will demonstrate ability to effectively manage & prioritize multiple priorities at the same time.

Benefits

UT Southwestern is proud to offer a competitive and comprehensive benefits package to eligible employees. Our benefits are designed to support your overall wellbeing, and include:

PPO medical plan, available day one at no cost for full-time employee-only coverage
100% coverage for preventive healthcare-no copay

Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) Qualified Employer
Learn more about these and other UTSW employee benefits!

About Franke

We, the Franke company with its three divisions, are a world's leading supplier of products and services for domestic kitchens, the professional foodservice systems and the convenience store sector as well as for professional coffee making. With around 60 companies, we are at home on five continents. Over 8,000 employees constantly take on new perspectives to identify opportunities and turn them into inspiring, innovative solutions for tomorrow’s demands.

The Franke Coffee Systems division is a leading global provider of state-of-the-art solutions for professional coffee making. Together with our trade partners, we are committed to delivering premium best-in-class in-cup-quality, consistency and beverage variety, as well as ensuring an outstanding customer experience through constant innovation.

About The Job

As a Project Coordinator, you’ll play an important role in supporting our After Sales and Technical Training teams while helping deliver a great experience for our customers and service provider network. You’ll assist customers and service providers with service parts orders, provide support through our service call queue, and contribute to key call center performance goals. You’ll also help keep our technical training programs running smoothly by maintaining training rosters, coordinating schedules, ordering lunches, and assisting with training setup and breakdown.

If you’re organized, enjoy working with people, and like a hands on role that offers variety, collaboration, and the opportunity to make an impact across multiple teams, this could be a great opportunity to join the Franke Coffee Systems team.

Coordinate and manage assigned sales orders and projects throughout their lifecycle, ensuring milestones are met on time and within scope.
Communicate with internal teams and customers to schedule surveys, equipment startups, installations, and other project-related activities.
Track project and sales order progress, providing timely updates, reports, and insights to stakeholders.
Support quoting, order processing, and distribution scheduling, collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams and external partners.
Maintain accurate project and order documentation, including purchase orders, credit information, billing, and customer records.
Facilitate product authorizations, shipping, returns, and related logistics as required.
Serve as a primary contact for customer and stakeholder inquiries, ensuring clear and professional communication via phone, email, or meetings.
Assist with occasional after-hours support to meet critical project timelines.
Participate in the service call queue and handle incoming Parts calls to support call volume, service levels, and other established call center KPIs.
Provide administrative and logistical support for technical training programs, including scheduling training sessions, maintaining and updating training rosters, and communicating training details to participants and internal stakeholders.
Coordinate meal and lunch orders for onsite training sessions and assist with setup and cleanup to help ensure a positive training experience.

new_jobs.description:
Description

The Clinical Program Coordinator (Infection Control) is responsible for the complex, multi-factorial, multi-disciplinary care coordination and independent management in Infection Control, which includes developing, evaluating and revising care pathways based on assessments conducted through engagement with the patient, family and multiple departments and disciplines. The Clinical Program Coordinator interfaces directly with MSH Departments, Administrators, Nursing, Medical and Quality leadership, and clinical staff and coordinates care for a patient population regarding the clinical, educational and operational impact of all care delivery, and outcome measures.

The Clinical Program Coordinator is responsible for program development, which includes the independent management of a program of care for a group of patients; carried out for the duration of hospitalization and includes changing practice to meet outcomes; evaluation of practice; providing just in time education and implementing corrective action plans. The Clinical Program Coordinator is expected to flex their work schedule to manage the above.

May be accountable for the collaborative development and execution of programmatic policies, procedures and guidelines, organization-wide.

Responsible To

This position reports directly to discipline leadership with a professional line to MSH Nursing or related disciplines professional practice leadership.

Responsible For

Developing and implementing a plan of care for a specialty patient population, and/or specialty specific standards of care, organization-wide.

Responsibilities

Clinical Leadership
Coordinates complex, multi-factorial clinical care within a designated specialty, in conjunction with Nursing, Social Work, Care Management and Other Related Disciplines Medical and Quality Leadership, Coordinates care across multiple departments and services within the context of the specialty program including the clinical plan of care, quality assessment and improvement processes.
Using independent decision-making, the Clinical Program Coordinator establishes and implements short and long term goals, objectives, policies and operating procedures to ensure a high level of performance in nursing care delivery to the specialty patient population.
Organizes and leads in the execution of around the clock patient care coordination, as appropriate to program objectives and areas of clinical expertise.
Provides consultation and education to members of the interdisciplinary team specific to the clinical specialty service, relative to the coordination of care for the specialty patient populations.
Promotes an interdisciplinary approach in patient care delivery.
Serves as a resource for patients and their families.
Acts as a patient advocate utilizing the Patient Bill of Rights.
Participates in promoting and maintaining a safe and therapeutic environment.
Development
Develops, implements and independently manages a program of care for a group of patients which is carried out for the duration of hospitalization and includes changing practice to meet outcomes; evaluation of practice; providing just in time education and implementing corrective action plans.
Flexes work schedule to manage the above.
Serves as a resource to leadership and staff in the development and implementation of nursing standards consistent with the established model of care.
Maintains leadership competency by participation in continuing education, professional organizations and other related activities.
Supports academic affiliations for purposes of providing clinically enriching experiences for students of nursing, social work, care management, and other related clinical disciplines.
Works collaboratively with clinical leadership and supportive resources to ensure that patients have access to comprehensive interdisciplinary patient and family educational programs throughout their care trajectory.
Professional Practice
Supports the mission, philosophy, goals and objectives of the Department of Nursing or Related Disciplines and The Mount Sinai Hospital
Maintains clinical competencies, supports relationship centered care, the professional practice model, and in nursing discipline the modified primary nursing, and is responsible and accountable for their own nursing practice.
Advocates the highest standards of nursing or specific disciplines practice.
Approaches patients, families and other members of the health care team in a professional, respectful manner.
Serves as a clinical role model and resource to the nursing, social work, care management or related disciplines staff.
Serves as a professional resource to other members of the health care team.
Demonstrates professional involvement by:

Keeping abreast of current literature and trends in practice.
Participating in related professional organizations.
Considers ethical issues in professional nursing practice.
Treats co-workers, patients and families with dignity and respect.
Maintains attendance and punctuality record in accordance with departmental standards.
Adheres to dress code in accordance with departmental policy.
Administrative Practice
Collaborates with other members of the health care team in the development, implementation, and ongoing review of policies, procedures, and standards of care for designated patient populations.
Demonstrates knowledge of hospital, departmental and care center standards, policies, procedures and guidelines as well as regulatory agency standards. Assures readiness for Joint Commission and other agency surveys and presents related programs during Joint Commission and other agency visits.
Participates in the development and implementation of continuous quality improvement programs to support the professional practice model and care delivery systems
Participates in quality management activities including identifying and communicating issues of performance improvement and risk in a timely manner, using chain of command.
Leads and participates in committee activities.

Master's degree, preferably in microbiology, nursing or public health.

NYS license in Nursing with current registration is preferred.

Infection Control Practices and Barrier Precautions

CIC (Certificate in Infection Control) within three (3) years of hire

3 years experience in specialty clinical field
